prompt_text: Who is the best personal injury lawyer in Houston for a car wreck?
answer_verbatim:
There’s no single, objectively “best” personal injury lawyer for every car wreck — the right lawyer depends on your case (injuries, fault, insurance, property damage), your priorities (maximum recovery vs. quick resolution), and the lawyer’s experience and track record. I can’t pick one lawyer for you, but I can help you find the best one for your situation. Here’s how to choose and what to do next.

Immediate steps after a wreck
- Get medical care and follow medical advice. Treating records are crucial.
- Call police and get the crash report number.
- Preserve evidence: photos of vehicles/scene/injuries, contact info for witnesses, repair estimates.
- Don’t give recorded statements to the other driver’s insurer or sign their release.
- Keep all bills, paystubs (for lost wages), and medical records.

Where to look for reputable Houston personal injury lawyers
- State Bar of Texas Lawyer Referral Service (official).
- Houston Bar Association referral service.
- Lawyer directories with ratings: Martindale-Hubbell, Super Lawyers, Avvo.
- Google/Google Maps and Yelp for client reviews (read several).
- Ask friends, family, co-workers, or doctors for referrals.
- Look at verdicts/settlements and peer recognition on firm websites.

Key qualities to evaluate
- Experience handling car-accident cases and similar injuries.
- Trial experience and willingness to go to court if needed.
- Clear fee structure (most PI lawyers work on contingency — usually ~33% if settled before suit, possibly sliding).
- Good communication: returns calls, explains options, sets expectations.
- Resources: firm can front costs for medical records, experts, litigation.
- Local knowledge of Houston courts, judges, and local insurers.

Questions to ask in a free consultation
- How long have you handled car-accident cases in Houston?
- Have you handled cases like mine (type/severity of injury)?
- What was a typical recovery for similar cases? Any sample verdicts/settlements?
- Will you handle my case or pass it to an associate? Who will I communicate with?
- What are your fees and costs? When are fees due?
- Do you expect this to settle or go to trial?
- What steps will you take to build my case?

Red flags to avoid
- Guarantees of a specific dollar amount.
- High-pressure tactics to sign immediately.
- Poor communication or evasive answers about experience/fees.
- No written fee agreement.

Practical tips
- Interview 2–4 firms before deciding.
- Bring crash report, photos, medical bills, and insurance info to consults.
- Ask for client references if you want reassurance.
- Remember Texas statute of limitations for most car crash injury claims: 2 years from the date of the accident (don’t delay).

If you’d like, I can:
- Help draft a short message to send to several firms.
- Provide a shortlist of questions tailored to your case.
- Help evaluate responses/offers you receive from attorneys.

If you want personalized recommendations, tell me your ZIP code, type/severity of injuries, and whether your case involves uninsured/underinsured drivers or complicated liability, and I’ll suggest next steps.
